paragraphs: The 320i has been a core petrol model in the 3 Series range for over a decade, spanning two generations under one badge. Early F30/F31 cars (2012 to 2015) use the N20 — a 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol engine introduced to replace the naturally aspirated straight-six in the 3 Series petrol lineup. From 2015, the F30/F31 320i switched to the B48, a newer 2.0-litre turbo four that's a different design entirely. The current G20/G21 generation (2019–present) continues with the B48, now in a further-evolved form. The 320i was discontinued in the UK after the 2024 model year update, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.
about.boldParagraph: The 320i is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol fitted to the F30/F31 320i from 2012 to 2015. Known for timing chain guide wear over time — see the callout above. We replace the timing chain, guides, tensioners and gaskets as standard on every N20 rebuild.

A 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol that replaced the N20 from 2015 onwards. Significantly more reliable than the N20, with no equivalent to the earlier engine's timing chain guide issue. We service it to the same standard as every other 4-cylinder rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the 320i spans two distinct engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an N20 part will work on a B48 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic 320i quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
